subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: DECISIVE HYDRATION ANSWER: (b). The user searched for stateToChange/hydrateChange and found nothing because the mapping is split across TWO named functions in store-temporal/shared.ts: mapTemporalChangeStateToChange (field-by-field producer, lines 87-124) and TEMPORAL_OWNED_PROJECTION_FIELDS (allowlist, lines 136-167), combined by projectTemporalStateOntoLatest (lines 174-184) into {...latest, ...temporalOwned}. Neither worker-bundle field appears in EITHER list. Every workflow-driven disk write (persistStateToDisk index.ts:266; refresh changes.ts:1573) routes through this stripping merge. ROOT CAUSE REFUTED AS STATED: the missing Change schema declaration is NOT why the evaluator sees undefined. ChangeSchema uses .passthrough() (changes.ts:1526), so unknown fields are preserved on read; the field simply never reaches disk JSON because the projection write strips it. The real cause is the projection allowlist/mapper omitting workerBundleProvenance. WHY THE SIBLING worker_bundle_impact WORKS: set_worker_bundle_impact writes disk DIRECTLY via store.changes.save({...change, worker_bundle_impact}) at change.ts:2955-2956 before firing the signal; the field lands on latest and survives subsequent {...latest,...temporalOwned} spreads. provenance_record has NO direct save (change.ts:2862-2878), so the field is never on latest and never persists. Latent finding: worker_bundle_impact itself is ALSO absent from the allowlist and survives only via the direct-save coupling; any future signal-only setter would lose it too.

The complete fix requires editing the projection allowlist + mapper (shared.ts) and declaring the field on ChangeSchema (types/changes.ts) + regenerating public schemas. sources.label: adv_run_test signal payload
sources.summary: evidence_kind is caller-supplied enum label passed through unvalidated. testRunRecorded records runId/exitCode/classification/command/durationMs/evidence_kind/quality only; records NO bundle generation, artifact hash, or source SHA. sources.label: adv_worker_bundle_provenance_record

sources.label: Evaluator match logic + source_sha nonblank-only check

sources.label: WorkerBundleManifest.generation is SHA-256 hex STRING; readWorkerBundleGeneration reads disk
sources.summary: generation is 64-hex-char string digest over worker.js+workflows.js. readWorkerBundleGeneration(bundleDir) reads from disk; returns null when manifest absent/invalid. Proves existence, not causation.

sources.label: Receipt field typed number — never wirable
sources.summary: worker_manifest_generation is z.number()/.optional() in three persisted/workflow-reachable shapes. 64-char hex string cannot parse as number; artifact binding never satisfiable. Dead field.

sources.label: Reducer + signalMutation (no type branching, no Zod validation)
sources.summary: applyWorkerBundleProvenanceRecordedToState copies field verbatim; no typeof check. signalMutation wraps handler without schema validation. No signal validator exists (grep validateSignal/signalValidator = 0).

sources.label: Bundle dir via import.meta.url (DEPLOYED dist); build run builds WORKTREE bundle
sources.summary: Worker child and host resolve dist/temporal/worker.js via import.meta.url (deployed). build_worker adv_run_test runs pnpm run build:worker in worktree cwd, producing WORKTREE bundle — different artifact/path than deployed bundle.

sources.label: Codebase replay-patch discipline
sources.summary: Every prior workflow state-shape/command-sequence change gated behind named PATCH marker to preserve replay determinism for pre-change histories. Bare type flip departs from this discipline.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: The proposed design (capture source_sha from HEAD + bundle generation from disk at RECORD time; reject caller-supplied authenticity values) is NECESSARY but INSUFFICIENT. Record-time capture proves a bundle EXISTS on disk and that HEAD is some commit; it does NOT prove the recorded build_worker RUN produced that bundle. The reproduction survives unchanged whenever a real (possibly stale) worktree bundle is present on disk — the normal state after any prior legitimate build. The temporal binding (run -> artifact) is entirely absent. The robust closure is for ADV to perform build+replay itself in one privileged tool that emits the receipt with ADV-captured anchors and ADV-owned run IDs, eliminating caller-supplied run IDs and the evidence_kind label as an authority channel. Even that leaves a residual: worktree-build provenance does not bind the separately-deployed trunk artifact.

blockers.finding: Core security claim false: design does not stop the true/true forgery. Capturing bundle generation at record time attests existence, not causation. With a stale-but-real worktree bundle on disk (normal post-build state), attacker running adv_run_test command:true evidence_kind:build_worker then ...replay_determinism then adv_worker_bundle_provenance_record records a receipt whose generation equals current on-disk generation and whose runs both exited 0 — gate passes. Evaluator (gate-readiness.ts:1080-1131) matches runId+evidence_kind+exitCode===0 and would additionally match generation==current, which holds because attacker never touched bundle. No file:line in proposed design establishes before/after-diff or ADV-owned-build binding.
blockers.in_scope_remediation: Either (a) ADV runs build:worker + replay itself in a single privileged tool emitting the receipt (preferred; eliminates caller-supplied run IDs + evidence_kind authority), or (b) capture worktree bundle generation immediately BEFORE the build_worker run and AFTER, and require the build run to have produced/refreshed the bundle (generation changed OR freshly created where null). Option (b) must handle deterministic no-op rebuilds explicitly to avoid false negatives. Without one of these, the gate remains forgeable.

source.label: Run record / evaluator / manifest reader
source.summary: run record carries no artifact binding; evaluator match logic is runId+kind+exitCode; readWorkerBundleGeneration reads whatever is on disk (existence, not causation).

validation.notes: Replay safety: bare number->string type flip on worker_manifest_generation will likely NOT raise TMPRL1100 (reducer at change-state.ts:1434-1449 does not branch on value type; no signal validator runs at workflow boundary). But it violates codebase patch-marker discipline (workflows.ts:1167-1198) and risks projection Zod parse (changes.ts:63) for any history storing a number. Conservative fix: NEW optional field worker_manifest_generation_sha:string alongside legacy number field, not type flip.

tradeoffs: ADV-owned build+replay tool is strongest closure but removes agent flexibility and centralizes a slow host-blocking operation (build:worker is heavy).
Before/after generation-diff keeps existing tool surface but cannot distinguish real deterministic no-op rebuild from `true` no-op without clean-tree precondition — fragile.
New-field approach is replay-safe and discipline-consistent but leaves dead legacy field and requires evaluator to read new field.
Worktree-bundle provenance cannot bind deployed trunk artifact (deploy runs post-merge from trunk) — inherent scope ceiling.

alternatives_considered.option: Proposed: capture anchors at record time, type-flip generation to string, evaluator verifies generation==current + source_sha==release commit
alternatives_considered.rationale: Does not bind run to artifact (blocker 1). source_sha==release-commit unimplementable at record time (merge commit does not exist yet — chicken-and-egg). Type flip replay-risky vs codebase discipline.

alternatives_considered.option: ADV-owned build+replay privileged tool emits the receipt (no caller run IDs)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Only design that structurally binds the build to the artifact it produced and removes evidence_kind as an authority channel. Heaviest to implement but closes the forgery class.

alternatives_considered.option: Before/after worktree-bundle generation diff across the build_worker run
alternatives_considered.rationale: Closes `true` forgery only with clean-tree/no-prior-bundle precondition; otherwise defeated by stale bundle and deterministic rebuilds. Weaker than ADV-owned build; fallback only.

alternatives_considered.option: New worker_manifest_generation_sha:string field instead of type flip
alternatives_considered.rationale: Replay-safe, matches existing patch discipline; required in addition to whichever binding fix is chosen.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Do NOT implement design as proposed. Two required changes: (1) close run->artifact binding via ADV-owned build+replay tool (preferred) or before/after generation-diff with clean-tree precondition; (2) use NEW optional string field for generation, not number->string flip. Update agreement to state residual: this gate attests worktree-build provenance only, not deployed-artifact provenance.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Return NEEDS_WORK to orchestrator. Design is directionally correct (server-captured anchors necessary) but as stated does not stop reported forgery and introduces replay-safety risk via type flip. Require run->artifact binding (ADV-owned build tool preferred) and new-field generation schema before implementation.
follow_ups: Confirm whether ADV-owned build:worker+replay tool acceptable given it blocks host on heavy build; if not, spec before/after generation-diff precondition precisely (clean tree? no prior bundle?).

documents.proposal:
## Intent

Make the worker-bundle release-provenance gate satisfiable. A recorded provenance receipt never reaches the disk projection the archive reads, so every change declaring `worker_bundle_impact: "required"` blocks forever.

## Root Cause Analysis

> **Correction:** an earlier revision of this RCA attributed the defect to a missing `Change` Zod schema declaration. Independent validation **refuted** that mechanism. `ChangeSchema` is declared `.passthrough()` (`plugin/src/types/changes.ts:1526`), so an unknown field present in disk JSON would survive parsing and reach the evaluator with no schema change at all. The direction was right — the field never reaches the evaluator — but the mechanism is on the **write** side, not the read side. The corrected analysis follows.

### Actual cause

Workflow-driven disk writes route through an explicit two-layer projection in `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/shared.ts`, and **both layers drop the field**:

| Layer | Location | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `mapTemporalChangeStateToChange` | `shared.ts:87-124` | Field-by-field producer, `ChangeWorkflowState` → `Change`. Does not emit `workerBundleProvenance`. |
| `TEMPORAL_OWNED_PROJECTION_FIELDS` | `shared.ts:136-167` | Allowlist of fields a Temporal dual-write may overwrite on disk. Does not list `workerBundleProvenance`. |
| `projectTemporalStateOntoLatest` | `shared.ts:174-184` | Merges `{ ...latest, ...temporalOwned }`, taking only allowlisted fields from the mapper output. |

Every workflow-driven write uses this path: `persistStateToDisk` (`store-temporal/index.ts:266-304`) calls `commitChangeProjection` with `mutateLatest: projectTemporalStateOntoLatest`; `store.changes.refresh` (`changes.ts:1573-1584`) reaches it via `dualWriteAfterMutation`.

The archive reads the **disk projection**, not the workflow — routine reads never query the workflow (`read-model.ts:44-82`), and the projection is parsed by `ChangeSchema` (`change-projection-reader.ts:408-411`). So `workflows.ts:737` genuinely returns the provenance, and it is genuinely discarded before disk.

### Why the sibling field appears to work

`worker_bundle_impact` is returned on the adjacent query line (`workflows.ts:736`) and does reach the archive — but **not** through the projection. `adv_change_set_worker_bundle_impact` writes disk directly via `store.changes.save({...change, worker_bundle_impact})` (`change.ts:2955-2956`) *before* firing its signal. The value lands on `latest`, and because it is absent from `temporalOwned`, the `{ ...latest, ...temporalOwned }` spread inherits it.

`adv_worker_bundle_provenance_record` (`change.ts:2862-2878`) fires its signal through `fireSignalAndRefresh` and performs **no** direct save. It depends entirely on the projection path, which strips the field.

**Latent defect:** `worker_bundle_impact` is *also* absent from the allowlist. It survives only through that direct-save coupling. Any future signal-only writer of impact would lose it the same way. This change fixes both fields rather than leaving the second trap armed.

### Empirical confirmation

- `jq` finds no `workerBundleProvenance` JSON path in **any** archived bundle. The four textual matches are prose inside proposals and spec deltas, not data.
- `fixArchivedProvenanceRecovery` — the change that introduced this chokepoint — archived on 2026-08-02 with `worker_bundle_impact.kind: "required"` and provenance absent. It shipped its own gate before that gate could apply to it.
- Reproduced 3× on `fixTaskUpdatePersistence`: record returns `success: true` with `recorded_at`; the immediately following archive returns `WORKER_BUNDLE_PROVENANCE_MISSING`. Attempts covered a plain record, a re-record, and re-confirming `worker_bundle_impact` to force a projection write. `source_sha` matched branch HEAD exactly every time.

### Why no test caught it

`change.worker-bundle.test.ts:122` owns the record tool but **mocks `fireSignalAndRefresh` to a no-op** (lines 22, 119) and asserts only the signal arguments. It never writes disk, never reads back, never runs the gate — it stops exactly one layer short of the defect. `gate-readiness.test.ts:2425+` hand-constructs state with provenance already set, bypassing the projection boundary entirely. `contracts.test.ts` covers the reducer and continue-as-new seed, which are workflow-state only.

No test exercises `signal → reduce → projection → disk → archive preflight`.

## LBP Targets

1. Add both `workerBundleProvenance` and `worker_bundle_impact` to the projection mapper and the owned-field allowlist, so the projection structurally mirrors workflow state (P33) rather than depending on a per-tool direct-save workaround.
2. Author a `WorkerBundleProvenanceSchema` — none exists standalone today. The signal payload schema (`signals.ts:266-272`) and the inline `ChangeWorkflowState` shape (`contracts.ts:751-757`) share the shape but are not reusable as the stored declaration.

## Agreement (rev 4 — authenticity scope split to a follow-up)

Scope returned to the delivered projection fix. The authenticity work explored in rev 2/rev 3 is split into a linked follow-up change; the evidence gathered is preserved below so the follow-up starts from a validated position rather than from scratch.

### Spec-law impact: No spec law update required

`rq-workerBundleReleaseProvenance01` already states the correct law, and scenario `.2` ("Required impact with valid provenance passes release") already asserts the behavior that was broken. This change restores conformance; it adds, modifies, and removes nothing.

### Objectives

- Make a recorded provenance receipt observable to the release-readiness evaluator, restoring conformance to `rq-workerBundleReleaseProvenance01.2`.
- Preserve every blocking path exactly: missing, incomplete, or failing-run receipts must still block.
- Add the round-trip regression coverage whose absence allowed this to ship.

### Acceptance criteria

1. `workerBundleProvenance` is declared on the `Change` schema so a persisted change can carry it, mirroring the sibling `worker_bundle_impact` declaration.
2. A provenance receipt recorded via `adv_worker_bundle_provenance_record` is observable to `evaluateWorkerBundleProvenanceForChange` when the archive evaluates a loaded `Change`.
3. A change with `worker_bundle_impact: "required"` and a valid receipt referencing passing build and replay runs completes release, satisfying `rq-workerBundleReleaseProvenance01.2`.
4. A change with `required` impact and no receipt still blocks with the existing declaration/missing blocker codes.
5. A receipt referencing a failing or unresolvable run still blocks.
6. `not_applicable` still skips the gate, and the typed declaration remains the applicability authority with no path heuristics.
7. Tracked public JSON schema artifacts regenerate deterministically and `schemas:check` stays green.
8. Full suite green.

### Constraints

1. No fail-open. The gate must keep blocking every case it blocks today except the genuinely-valid one.
2. No relaxation of run validation; referenced build and replay runs must still resolve and have passed.
3. No path heuristics or file inspection as an applicability fallback.
4. Preserve existing blocker codes and reason shapes consumed by `archive-gate.ts`.

### Avoidances and out of scope

- Retroactive provenance backfill for already-archived changes.
- Changes to `worker_bundle_impact` classification semantics.
- Post-deployment or runtime freshness, explicitly out of scope per the requirement body.
- Reconciling the 17 blocked changes; this change makes their release possible but does not perform it.
- **Evidence authenticity — split to a linked follow-up change.** See below.

### Known limitation: positive evidence is weak (deferred, not accepted silently)

This change makes the gate *function*. It does not make the gate's positive evidence *trustworthy*. Acceptance-stage security review found the gate is satisfiable with forged evidence, and adversarial design validation confirmed the fix is materially larger than this change's scope.

Reproduction, verified:

```
adv_run_test  command: "true"  evidence_kind: "build_worker"       -> exit 0
adv_run_test  command: "true"  evidence_kind: "replay_determinism" -> exit 0
adv_worker_bundle_provenance_record  source_sha: <any nonblank string>
-> gate passes; no worker built, no replay verified
```

Because `evidence_kind` is caller-supplied (`tools/test.ts:386`, passed through unvalidated at 534-535) and `source_sha` is caller-supplied (`tools/change.ts:2801`) and only nonblank-checked (`temporal/gate-readiness.ts:1068`).

This weakness is **pre-existing** in the verifier and the evidence-recording surface, none of which this change touches. This change does not introduce it; it makes it reachable by repairing the gate's positive path. Before this change the gate rejected valid and invalid receipts identically, so it had never verified a worker bundle at all.

Deferred deliberately because the validated fix requires ADV to perform the build and replay itself in a dedicated privileged tool — a new execution model with an unresolved host-blocking/timeout problem — which is a different problem from the projection defect this change repairs, and which would keep 17 changes blocked while it is solved.

Findings carried to the follow-up so it does not restart from scratch:

- Capture-at-record-time is insufficient. It proves the bundle exists, not that the recorded runs built it; a stale-but-real bundle from any prior build defeats it.
- The run-to-artifact binding must be causal: ADV performs build and replay and emits the receipt with ADV-owned run identifiers.
- `worker_manifest_generation` must not be type-flipped from number to string. It appears in three persisted shapes and the repository gates state-shape changes behind named replay patches; add a new optional string field instead.
- The canonical bundle path is the worktree bundle at `<worktree>/plugin/dist/temporal/`, not the deployed bundle resolved via `import.meta.url`, which is a different artifact.
- `source_sha` cannot be matched against the release/merge commit, which does not exist at record time; matching worktree HEAD at evaluation time is the implementable form.
- Residual risk that remains even after the follow-up: worktree-build provenance is not deployed-artifact provenance, and a generation hash is not source-review provenance.

## Design

Validated by independent researcher: **NEEDS_WORK** on the original schema-only approach, with a concrete recommended alternative. Option B (structural) adopted below.

### D1 — Project both fields, not just the broken one

`plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/shared.ts`:

- **Mapper** (`shared.ts:93-124`): emit `worker_bundle_impact: safeState.worker_bundle_impact` and `workerBundleProvenance: safeState.workerBundleProvenance`.
- **Allowlist** (`shared.ts:136-167`): add `"worker_bundle_impact"` and `"workerBundleProvenance"`.

Both fields are included deliberately. `worker_bundle_impact` currently survives only because `adv_change_set_worker_bundle_impact` happens to direct-save before signaling; that is an accidental coupling, not a design. Fixing only provenance would leave an identical trap armed for any future signal-only writer.

**Casing is preserved as-is** (`worker_bundle_impact` snake, `workerBundleProvenance` camel). The inconsistency is pre-existing and cosmetic; renaming either would break replay histories.

**Rejected — Option A (minimal):** add `store.changes.save({...change, workerBundleProvenance})` to the record tool, mirroring the impact setter. Smaller diff, but it propagates the per-tool workaround, leaves the allowlist gap intact, and keeps the projection structurally out of sync with workflow state. Rejected per P33: make correctness structural, not per-caller.

### D2 — Author the stored schema

`plugin/src/types/changes.ts`, beside `WorkerBundleImpactSchema` (~1470):

```ts
export const WorkerBundleProvenanceSchema = z.object({
  source_sha: z.string(),
  build_run_id: z.string(),
  replay_run_id: z.string(),
  worker_manifest_generation: z.number().optional(),
  recorded_at: z.string(),
});
```

Shape mirrors the signal payload (`signals.ts:266-272`) and the inline `ChangeWorkflowState` declaration (`contracts.ts:751-757`). Added to `ChangeSchema` as `workerBundleProvenance: WorkerBundleProvenanceSchema.optional()`.

Note this is **not** what unblocks the gate — `.passthrough()` at `types/changes.ts:1526` already preserves unknown fields on read. The declaration is for type safety and public-schema accuracy, so the field is a first-class part of the contract rather than an undeclared passenger.

### D3 — Regenerate public schemas

`ChangeSchema` is public via `schema-registry.ts:37-41` → `change.schema.json`. Run `pnpm run schemas:generate`; keep `pnpm run schemas:check` green. No new registry entry required — it already points at `ChangeSchema`.

### D4 — Close the round-trip test gap

The defect's real signature is a **boundary crossing that no test crosses**. Mirror `spec-deltas.disk-projection.test.ts`, which already covers `projectTemporalStateOntoLatest` for deltas:

- Record provenance through the real signal path (not a mocked `fireSignalAndRefresh`).
- Reload the `Change` from disk.
- Assert `evaluateWorkerBundleProvenanceForChange` / `getArchiveGatePreflightError` passes.

Also tighten `change.worker-bundle.test.ts:122`, which mocks `fireSignalAndRefresh` at lines 22/119 and stops one layer short. It owns the record tool and should not be able to pass while the recorded value never persists.

### D5 — Preserve every blocking branch

Validator confirmed all blocking paths in `evaluateWorkerBundleProvenance` (`gate-readiness.ts:1020-1132`) remain reachable once `provenance` is defined:

| Branch | Location |
|---|---|
| Missing receipt | `1055-1066` |
| Incomplete (no `source_sha`) | `1068-1078` |
| Unresolved run IDs | `1080-1107` |
| Failing runs (`exitCode !== 0`) | `1109-1129` |
| `not_applicable` without rationale | `1043-1053` |
| Undeclared impact | `~1024-1037` |

`test_runs` already projects correctly (allowlist `144`, mapper `101`), so run validation works end-to-end today. The only behavioral change is the intended one: a complete receipt referencing passing runs now passes. **No fail-open introduced.**

### D6 — Campsite

`changeSeedStateFromChange` (`change-state.ts:198-265`) casts a `Change` through `Partial<Pick<ChangeWorkflowState, "workerBundleProvenance" | ...>>` to read the field. Once it is a real `Change` field the cast is redundant and may be simplified. No type collision — both declarations share the same shape. Optional; not required for correctness.

### Verification strategy

- **RED:** record provenance through the real path, reload from disk, assert the field is absent / the gate blocks. Must fail before the fix.
- **GREEN:** same test passes after mapper + allowlist changes.
- Regression: missing receipt still blocks.
- Regression: receipt with unresolvable run IDs still blocks.
- Regression: receipt referencing a failing run still blocks.
- Regression: `not_applicable` still skips.
- `worker_bundle_impact` still reaches the archive after being added to the allowlist (guards against the direct-save path and the projection path conflicting).
- `pnpm run schemas:check` green after regeneration.
- Full suite green.

### Residual risk

Adding `worker_bundle_impact` to the allowlist changes which writer wins when both the direct save and the projection carry a value. Both derive from the same declaration, so they should agree — but the regression test above exists specifically to prove that, since a disagreement would silently overwrite an operator's declaration.

# Executive Summary

## Outcome

A safety check that was supposed to confirm a piece of infrastructure had been rebuilt and tested was rejecting every change, including correct ones. It now works. You are approving a repair that unblocks 17 pieces of completed work which could not be released.

## Why It Matters

Seventeen changes were finished but stuck — they could not complete release because the check refused all evidence, valid or not. This repair releases that backlog. It also closes the gap in testing that allowed the fault to ship unnoticed.

One limitation is carried forward deliberately and is described under Remaining Concerns.

## Verdict

APPROVED

## What Was Built

1. Recorded evidence is now saved where the release check can see it. Previously it was written to one place and read from another, so the check never found it (the disk projection dropped the field).
2. A related field was fixed at the same time. It only appeared to work because a different part of the system happened to write it separately — any future change to how it was recorded would have lost it the same way.
3. The published data format was regenerated to match, verified reproducible.
4. A test was added that follows evidence all the way from recording to the release check. No test previously crossed that boundary, which is why the fault shipped.
5. Tests were added confirming the check still refuses incomplete, missing, and failed evidence.

## What Was Verified

- Verdict: APPROVED with 0 blockers and 0 issues in the shipped scope.
- Tests: full suite passed, zero failures. Every code change was proven by first writing a test that failed, then making it pass.
- Preview URL: not_applicable — no user-facing or visual output; all changes are internal data-handling and release-checking logic.
- Contract matrix: 12 of 12 required rows passed or respected, 0 failing.

## Remaining Concerns

**Non-blocking, disclosed, and assigned to a follow-up change.** The check now works, but the evidence it accepts is weaker than it appears. A person or agent could run a command that does nothing, label it "the build", and satisfy the check. Nothing verifies the command did what the label claims.

This weakness already existed and is not introduced here — but before this repair the check rejected everything, so it was unreachable. Repairing the check makes it reachable.

It was investigated during review. An initial fix was designed, independently challenged, and **proven not to work** — it would have added ceremony while leaving the gap open. The design that does work requires the system to perform the build itself, a materially larger piece of work with an unresolved timing problem. On that evidence the decision was to release this repair now and address evidence trustworthiness separately, rather than keep 17 changes blocked.

Everything learned, including the design proven wrong, is recorded so the follow-up starts from a validated position.

## Supporting Evidence

Tasks tk-853702694f84, tk-0f7410ffe9b7, tk-e314f51294f0, tk-cbff6085c204, tk-214f5645a3ab. Full suite tr_msdulghd_868c6801; checks tr_msduh78y_e649b046; earlier full suite tr_msdppwn2_616813b1. Two independent reviewer approvals. Three independent scanner reviews at acceptance. Two adversarial design validations, the second refuting the proposed authenticity fix. Contract review matrix, 12 rows, 0 failing.

## Release Readiness Summary

Release-ready. Hardening found no blocking defects and closed the three test-coverage findings raised at review, so nothing actionable remains open against this change.

The repair itself is small and contained: three hand-edited source files plus regenerated data format and tests. It touches no configuration, no database migrations, no external services, and no deployment pipeline, so there is nothing operational to prepare or roll back.

One sequencing point matters for release. This change is subject to the very check it repairs, so it cannot complete release until it is merged and the plugin is redeployed. That ordering is deliberate — declaring the change exempt to sidestep the check would be the exact shortcut this work exists to prevent.

Verification: full suite passed with zero failures; all quality checks passed with zero errors; a dry-run merge into the default branch was clean.

## Approval Consequence Context

1. **Delivered value** — pass. Release check repaired; 17 blocked changes become releasable. Source: contract matrix 12/12, task implementation summaries.
2. **Enabling-only / follow-up dependency** — pass. Makes release possible; does not perform the backlog reconciliation. Source: agreement out-of-scope.
3. **Ops readiness** — pass. No env vars, migrations, external services, CI/CD, or infrastructure touched; cleanup scan found no temp files, debug code, or dead imports. Source: harden deployment and cleanup scans.
4. **Migration / data impact** — n/a. Schema change is additive-optional; existing records remain valid and replay-safe. Source: reviewer confirmation on additive-optional shape, no migration surface in diff.
5. **Frontend / preview impact** — not_applicable. No user-facing or visual output. Source: Preview URL Proof and matching contract matrix rationale.
6. **Collision / release risk** — warning. Dry-run merge into the default branch is clean and the branch is level with it. One other active change overlaps a file but sits 767 commits behind and needs a large rebase regardless. Source: harden merge-compatibility check, review branch comparison.
7. **Open follow-ups** — warning. One substantive and non-blocking: `bindProvenanceEvidence`, carrying the verified reproduction, the design proven wrong, and six established constraints. The three review coverage findings were fixed during hardening, not deferred.
8. **Next action** — `/adv-archive fixWorkerBundleProvenanceGate`. Release completion additionally requires merge and redeploy because of the bootstrap noted above.
